original_value: Education competitiveness is a key feature of national competitiveness. It is crucial for nations to develop and enhance student and teacher potential to increase national competitiveness. The decreasing population of children has caused a series of social problems in many developed countries, directly affecting education and com.petitiveness in an international environment. In Taiwan, a low birthrate has had a large impact on schools at every level because of a substantial decrease in enrollment and a surplus of teachers. Therefore, close attention must be paid to these trends. In this study, combining a whale optimization algorithm (WOA) and support vector regression (WOASVR) was proposed to determine trends of student and teacher numbers in Taiwan for higher accuracy in time-series forecasting analysis. To select the most suitable support vector kernel parameters, WOA was applied. Data collected from the Ministry of Education datasets of student and teacher numbers between 1991 and 2018 were used to examine the proposed method. Analysis revealed that the numbers of students and teachers decreased annually except in private primary schools. A comparison of the forecasting results obtained from WOASVR and other common models indicated that WOASVR provided the lowest mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and root mean square error (RMSE) for all analyzed datasets. Forecasting performed using the WOASVR method can provide accurate data for use in developing education policies and responses.

result.paraphrase: Educational competitiveness is a major component of national competitiveness. To strengthen a country’s competitiveness, it is essential to cultivate and improve the abilities of students and teachers. In many developed countries, the decline in the child population has triggered various social issues, directly influencing education and competitiveness in the global arena. In Taiwan, the low birthrate has significantly affected schools across all levels due to sharp enrollment declines and an excess of teachers. Accordingly, these trends require close attention. This study proposed combining a whale optimization algorithm (WOA) with support vector regression (WOASVR) to more accurately forecast trends in the numbers of students and teachers in Taiwan through time-series analysis. WOA was used to choose the most suitable support vector kernel parameters. The proposed approach was evaluated using Ministry of Education data on student and teacher numbers from 1991 to 2018. The analysis showed that student and teacher numbers declined each year, except in private primary schools. A comparison between WOASVR and other common forecasting models showed that WOASVR achieved the lowest mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and root mean square error (RMSE) across all datasets analyzed. Forecasts produced by the WOASVR method can offer accurate information to support education policy development and responses.
